narrative.overview:
Paper, ink, and one blue pen. Slate looks like a financial record kept by somebody competent and kind: a warm beige page, graphite writing, numbers that line up so they can be scanned rather than read, and exactly one blue mark showing what to do next. The warmth comes from the paper itself, never from decoration.

The restraint is meant to read as competence rather than as coldness. There is no bolder weight to reach for, no second action colour to escalate to, and no motion that is not carrying information. When a screen needs to feel more serious, it gets quieter, not louder.

The same world covers a consumer booking flow with room to breathe and internal tables carrying 136 rows of live roster. It holds together because both are the same ledger at different zoom levels.
keyCharacteristics: Beige and white surfaces dominate; navy appears as an occasional band.
Sky is the only action colour, and its rarity is what makes it work.
Numbers are tabular wherever they can be compared.
Depth is a soft shadow in light and a border in dark, never a hard drop.
Nothing animates unless the motion is the message.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Sky is the only colour that may mean "do this". Yellow, mint and peach are illustration accents and may never carry a call to action. If two things on a screen are competing to be the next action, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Measured Pairing Rule
rules.body: No single colour clears the 3:1 a focus indicator needs on both a beige page and a sky button, so the focus line is chosen by the surface it lands on: brand blue on light, sky on navy, graphite on a sky fill. Every pairing is measured in scripts/test-contrast.ts, and the colours that do NOT clear are kept there as tripwires.

rules.name: The No Black Rule
rules.body: There is no hard black anywhere, including in shadows. Graphite is as dark as text goes and shadow colours are tinted with the warm neutrals.

rules.name: The 600 Ceiling Rule
rules.body: PP Mori ships 200, 400 and 600. Medium is not used and 700 is aliased to 600, so there is no bolder weight to reach for. Emphasis comes from size, colour or space. font-synthesis: none is set so the browser cannot fake one.

rules.name: The Ledger Numerals Rule
rules.body: Anything a reader might compare down a column gets tabular numerals: rates, payments, counts, durations, times and dates. A figure that jumps sideways as it updates is a defect.

rules.name: The Plain Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case with no letter spacing. Uppercase tracked labels read as institutional, which is the opposite of the voice.

rules.name: The Prose Width Rule
rules.body: The 65ch limit goes on the paragraph, never on the container that holds a table or a grid of controls.

rules.name: The Shadow Swap Rule
rules.body: A card's edge is carried by a shadow in light and by a border in dark. Any component relying on a shadow to be legible needs a border under dark:, or it dissolves into the page. Dark borders are stronger than light's hairline because in dark they are the only thing separating a field from its card, and an input boundary has to clear 3:1.

rules.name: The Pills Are Badges Rule
rules.body: A fully rounded shape means "this is a status", never "this is a button". Buttons are 12px or 16px. A pill shaped button steals the affordance from the real controls on the screen.

dos: Do reserve sky for the single next action on a screen, and let its rarity do the work.
Do put tabular numerals on anything a reader could compare down a column.
Do add a border under dark: to anything whose edge is carried by a shadow in light.
Do measure a new colour pairing in scripts/test-contrast.ts before shipping it, including against the sky wash and the sky fill, not just against the page.
Do give every control at least 44px of height, and mark state with shape or weight as well as colour.
Do keep the 65ch reading limit on the paragraph and off the container.
donts: Don't use yellow, mint or peach for a call to action. They are illustration accents.
Don't reach for a weight above 600, or let the browser synthesise one.
Don't put white text on the sky fill. It measures 1.56:1. The label on sky is always graphite, in both themes.
Don't use a hard black, in text or in a shadow.
Don't make a button a pill. Pills are badges.
Don't uppercase or letter space a label.
Don't animate anything whose motion is not carrying information, and never animate a table of rows on load.
Don't let a component depend on its parent for its spacing or its ring; a component that only looks right inside one particular parent is broken at the next call site.
